quests.instruction: Touch the tool we use to color a picture, not to write words!
quests.question: Crayon
quests.hint: It can melt if it gets too warm in the sun.
quests.explanation: Well done! Crayons come in many colors so every picture can look different.
quests.funFact: One box of crayons can have more than sixty different colors inside!

quests.instruction: Touch the table where your pencils and notebook sit during class!
quests.question: Desk
quests.hint: You place your notebook and pencil on it before you start writing.
quests.explanation: Well done! A desk gives every student their own space to work.
quests.funFact: Some classrooms use desks that can be pushed together to make small groups!

quests.instruction: Find the tool you hold to draw a picture of your family!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: It leaves a soft grey line when it touches your page.
quests.explanation: Well done! A pencil makes marks that an eraser can rub away later.
quests.funFact: The soft grey part inside a pencil is called graphite, not lead at all!

quests.instruction: Touch the item we open to read words and look at pictures!
quests.question: Book
quests.hint: It can tell you a story about dragons, animals, or faraway places.
quests.explanation: Well done! A book can teach us new things or tell a fun story.
quests.funFact: The very first books were written by hand, long before printing was invented!

quests.instruction: Touch the bag that lives inside our backpack, full of writing tools!
quests.question: Pencil Case
quests.hint: It holds your pencils, eraser, and ruler all in one place.
quests.explanation: Well done! A pencil case keeps our desk neat and organized.
quests.funFact: Some pencil cases can stand up on their own like a little box!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool that keeps our lines from going wobbly!
quests.question: Ruler
quests.hint: It can tell you how many centimeters long your pencil is.
quests.explanation: Well done! A ruler has numbers that show us the length of things.
quests.funFact: Rulers can measure in centimeters on one side and inches on the other!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool with a handle for each of your fingers!
quests.question: Scissors
quests.hint: It has two blades that open and close like a little mouth.
quests.explanation: Correct! Scissors are always used slowly and carefully in the classroom.
quests.funFact: School scissors often have rounded tips to help keep little fingers safe!

quests.instruction: Point to the seat every student has next to their desk!
quests.question: Chair
quests.hint: It usually has four legs, a seat, and a back to lean on.
quests.explanation: Correct! A chair and a desk almost always sit right next to each other.
quests.funFact: Some classroom chairs are stacked together and stored when they're not needed!

quests.instruction: Point to the pouch that keeps your desk neat and tidy!
quests.question: Pencil Case
quests.hint: It usually has a zipper to keep everything safely inside.
quests.explanation: Correct! A pencil case travels inside your backpack with all your tools.
quests.funFact: A tidy pencil case can help you find your pencil in just one second!

quests.instruction: Point to the item students use to write notes during a lesson!
quests.question: Notebook
quests.hint: Its pages start out empty until you fill them with your writing.
quests.explanation: Correct! A notebook's pages are blank until a student fills them up.
quests.funFact: Writing in a notebook every day is a great way to practice new words!

quests.instruction: Point to the bag we pack with pencils, books, and snacks each morning!
quests.question: Backpack
quests.hint: You wear this bag on your back with two straps over your shoulders.
quests.explanation: Correct! A backpack keeps our school things together in one safe place.
quests.funFact: Some backpacks have a special pocket just the right size for a water bottle!

quests.instruction: Point to the flat surface where a student sits down to work!
quests.question: Desk
quests.hint: It is flat on top, just the right size to hold your books.
quests.explanation: Correct! A desk is where a student's books and pencils usually sit.
quests.funFact: The word desk comes from an old word meaning a table for writing!

quests.instruction: Point to the thing we borrow from a library to read at home!
quests.question: Book
quests.hint: It has a cover, and inside are many pages full of words.
quests.explanation: Correct! A book is the perfect place to find your favorite story.
quests.funFact: Some books have thousands of pages, while others have only a few!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool with little marks that tells us how long things are!
quests.question: Ruler
quests.hint: It helps your lines look perfectly straight, never wobbly.
quests.explanation: Correct! A ruler stops our lines from turning out crooked.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people used their own feet and hands to measure things before rulers!

quests.instruction: Point to the soft, waxy stick children use most for coloring!
quests.question: Crayon
quests.hint: It feels waxy and comes in a big box of many bright colors.
quests.explanation: Correct! A crayon colors a picture, while a pencil is better for writing words.
quests.funFact: Crayons are made from wax, which is why they melt in hot sunshine!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool that needs sharpening when its tip gets round!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: You need to sharpen its tip so it can write again.
quests.explanation: Correct! Every student uses a pencil to practice writing every day.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people wrote with sticks and feathers before pencils were invented!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool that cleans up pencil marks so you can try again!
quests.question: Eraser
quests.hint: Pencils often carry a tiny piece of it on their top end.
quests.explanation: Correct! An eraser is a student's best friend when a letter looks wrong.
quests.funFact: Before rubber erasers, people used soft bread to rub out pencil marks!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool that helps our art projects stay stuck in place!
quests.question: Glue Stick
quests.hint: You twist it up like a small tube before you rub it on paper.
quests.explanation: Correct! A glue stick is perfect for sticking paper without any mess.
quests.funFact: A glue stick dries clear, so you can barely see it on your paper!

quests.instruction: Touch the flat table where we keep our books and do our work!
quests.question: Desk
quests.hint: A chair usually sits right beside it, ready for you to sit down.
quests.explanation: Yes! A desk is the flat table where we sit to write and learn.
quests.funFact: Some classrooms use desks that can be pushed together to make small groups!

quests.instruction: Touch the piece of furniture we sit on at our desk!
quests.question: Chair
quests.hint: You pull it out before you sit down at your desk.
quests.explanation: Yes! A chair is what we sit on at our desk in the classroom.
quests.funFact: Chairs have been used by people for thousands of years, even in ancient times!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool we twist open to stick our paper crafts together!
quests.question: Glue Stick
quests.hint: It feels a little bit sticky after you rub it on your page.
quests.explanation: Yes! A glue stick makes paper sticky so our crafts stay together.
quests.funFact: Glue sticks were made so children could glue paper without sticky, messy fingers!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool with two blades that we use to cut paper!
quests.question: Scissors
quests.hint: You put your fingers in its handles and squeeze to make it cut.
quests.explanation: Yes! Scissors have two blades that we use to cut paper carefully.
quests.funFact: The very first scissors were shaped very differently from the ones we use today!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool that helps your paper look neat after a mistake!
quests.question: Eraser
quests.hint: It is soft and a little bit stretchy in your hand.
quests.explanation: Yes! An eraser rubs pencil marks off your paper so you can try again.
quests.funFact: Erasers are made from rubber, which is why they can bend and squish!

quests.instruction: Touch the colorful stick we use to draw bright, colorful pictures!
quests.question: Crayon
quests.hint: You press it on paper to fill a picture with color, not words.
quests.explanation: Yes! A crayon is the waxy stick we use to color our pictures.
quests.funFact: One box of crayons can have more than sixty different colors inside!

quests.instruction: Touch the thing full of pages and pictures that we read every day!
quests.question: Book
quests.hint: You open it and turn each page to find out what happens next.
quests.explanation: Yes! A book is full of pages we read for stories and learning.
quests.funFact: The very first books were written by hand, long before printing was invented!

quests.instruction: Touch the straight tool we lay flat on paper before drawing a line!
quests.question: Ruler
quests.hint: It is long, flat, and has little lines and numbers along one edge.
quests.explanation: Yes! A ruler helps us draw straight lines and measure how long things are.
quests.funFact: Rulers can measure in centimeters on one side and inches on the other!

quests.instruction: Touch the little bag that keeps our pencils and erasers together!
quests.question: Pencil Case
quests.hint: It is small enough to fit right inside your backpack.
quests.explanation: Yes! A pencil case keeps our pencils, erasers, and rulers together in one spot.
quests.funFact: Some pencil cases can stand up on their own like a little box!

quests.instruction: Touch the item with blank pages where we write our own words!
quests.question: Notebook
quests.hint: It often has lines inside to help your writing stay neat.
quests.explanation: Yes! A notebook has empty pages where we write our own words and ideas.
quests.funFact: Some notebooks have a spiral of wire so the pages can turn easily!

quests.instruction: Touch the bag we wear on our shoulders to carry our school things!
quests.question: Backpack
quests.hint: It has zippers and pockets to keep your school things safe inside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A backpack carries our books and supplies safely to and from school.
quests.funFact: Backpacks have two straps so the weight spreads evenly across both shoulders!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool a student uses first to practice writing letters!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: You hold it between your fingers and press it gently on paper.
quests.explanation: Yes! A pencil is the tool we use to write words and draw pictures.
quests.funFact: The soft grey part inside a pencil is called graphite, not lead at all!
